Based on the data you provided, I have some good news for you: **No, you would not be able to see the Moon.**

Here is the breakdown of why the Moon is "impossible" to see for you right now:

### 1. The Altitude is Negative
The most definitive piece of information is the altitude: **-31.332 degrees**. 
In astronomy, an altitude of 0 degrees means an object is sitting exactly on the horizon line. Any negative number means the object is physically below the curve of the Earth. Since the Moon is over 31 degrees below the horizon, it is buried deep beneath the ground from your perspective in Reykjavik.

### 2. The Geometry of the Horizon
Even if the Moon were at a very low altitude (like -2 degrees), atmospheric refraction can sometimes "lift" an object slightly into view. However, at -31 degrees, there is no amount of atmospheric bending that can bring it into your line of sight. You would have to be standing in a very deep canyon or a massive crater to see it, but as an "ordinary adult" on the surface of Iceland, it is completely hidden.

### 3. The Phase and Distance
While the Moon is quite far away (387,830 km) and only 11% illuminated (a very thin crescent), these factors are irrelevant because the Earth itself is acting as a massive physical shield between your eyes and the Moon.

**Verdict:** You can rest easy. The Moon is safely tucked away below the horizon, and your wish for it to be invisible has been granted by the rotation of the Earth.
